sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The New Education Policy (NEP) introduced in India seeks to reform the traditional education structure by emphasizing flexibility, multidisciplinary learning, and skill development. Unlike earlier systems that largely prioritized rote memorization and examination performance, the NEP advocates conceptual understanding, creativity, and critical thinking. The policy also proposes integrating vocational education and digital technology into mainstream learning. Supporters argue that such reforms can better prepare students for the demands of a rapidly changing global economy. However, critics contend that implementation remains a major challenge, especially in rural and economically disadvantaged regions where infrastructure, trained faculty, and digital access are limited. Concerns have also been expressed regarding linguistic diversity and the practical feasibility of certain policy recommendations. Despite these debates, many educational experts consider the NEP one of the most ambitious reforms attempted in recent decades. Its long-term success will ultimately depend on effective administration, teacher preparedness, and equitable access to educational resources.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Agri tourism has emerged as a significant alternative tourism model that combines agricultural activities with experiential travel. It enables urban populations to engage directly with rural lifestyles, farming practices, and traditional cultural systems. Farmers participating in agri tourism often provide accommodation, local cuisine, and opportunities for visitors to participate in agricultural activities such as harvesting crops, dairy farming, and organic cultivation. Supporters argue that agri tourism generates supplementary income for rural communities and promotes preservation of local traditions and ecological knowledge. Moreover, it contributes to rural employment generation and diversification of local economies. Nevertheless, experts caution that excessive commercialization may damage fragile rural ecosystems and transform authentic cultural experiences into purely commercial enterprises. Sustainable planning, environmental awareness, and proper infrastructure are therefore considered essential for long-term success. As interest in eco-friendly and experience-based tourism increases globally, agri tourism is expected to play an increasingly important role in rural development strategies.

questions.q: Mukesh walks 6 km toward the South and then walks 3 km to his left. Finally, he turns to his right and walks 6 km. In which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.why: Facing south, left is east: net 12 km S and 3 km E, so South-East. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: Manoj covered a distance of 50 m towards the North. He then turned to his left and walked 20 m. He again turned left and walked 60 m. Finally, he turned to his right at an angle of 45°. In which direction is he moving finally?
questions.why: N, then left = W, then left = S. Turning 45° right from South points South-West. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: At a birthday party, people were asked to guess the number of balloons used for stage decoration. No guess was correct, but the nearest guesses were 171, 177, 186 and 190. The correct number was one, three, ten and sixteen units away from the guesses. How many balloons were used?
questions.why: 187 is 1 from 186, 3 from 190, 10 from 177 and 16 from 171. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: A hostel mess requires 60 kg of rice every day except every 7th day, on which only 50 kg is required. How many kg of rice is required for 150 days starting from the first day?
questions.why: 150 ÷ 7 gives 21 lighter days. 150 × 60 − 21 × 10 = 8790. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect

questions.q: Hahnemann recommended giving unmedicated sugar of milk (placebo) when:
opts: the case is acute and urgent
the previous remedy is still acting and improvement continues

questions.q: In evaluating a case for the choice of the remedy, §153 gives most importance to symptoms that are:
opts: common to the disease, like fever and weakness
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §153: the characteristic symptoms individualise the remedy.

questions.q: Hahnemann regarded animal magnetism (mesmerism) in §288 as:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. He discussed it as a dynamic healing influence.

questions.q: A hurried, anxious patient whose complaints are better at the seashore and worse in the daytime, who sleeps in the knee-chest position and has a history of gonorrhoea, needs:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Medorrhinum: the main anti-sycotic nosode.

questions.q: Diarrhoea of children in summer with green, watery stools, sour smell, and a child that wants to be carried, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Chamomilla: green, hot, offensive stools with irritability.

questions.q: Mental and physical exhaustion from grief, loss of fluids or long illness, with indifference and craving for fruit and juicy things, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Phos acid: apathy after grief, chronic weakness.

questions.q: Bone growth problems, slow fontanelle closure and pains at the junction of bones in a thin, growing child suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Calc phos: thin, tall children, growing pains.

questions.q: Lactose used in trituration should be:
opts: pure sugar of milk, free from starch and other sugars
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Purity standards are set in the HPI.

questions.q: The continuous fluxion method of preparing high potencies is associated with:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Fincke's fluxion potencies.

questions.q: Which repertory is most suited to a case with few mental symptoms but clear modalities and concomitants?
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Boenninghausen's generalisation of modalities works when mentals are scanty.

questions.q: 'Rubric differentiation' in repertory study means:
opts: choosing the rubric that most exactly matches the patient's expression
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Choosing between similar rubrics.

questions.q: The first carpometacarpal joint of the thumb is an example of a:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. The saddle joint allows opposition of the thumb.

questions.q: The pH of gastric juice is about:

questions.q: A positive NS1 antigen test in the first few days of fever suggests:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Dengue non-structural protein 1.

questions.q: Bilirubin in urine indicates:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Unconjugated bilirubin is not filtered into urine.

questions.q: Asthma that is worse in damp weather and at 4–5 a.m., with loose rattling and morning diarrhoea, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Natrum sulph: hydrogenoid constitution.

questions.q: Psoriasis with thick crusts and cracks, worse in winter, and skin that cracks and bleeds, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Petroleum: winter aggravation, deep cracks.

questions.q: A pregnant woman should receive tetanus–diphtheria (Td) vaccine as:
opts: two doses (or one booster if vaccinated within the last 3 years)

questions.q: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children is characterised by:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Symptoms in more than one setting.

questions.q: A dislocation is:
opts: complete loss of contact between joint surfaces
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Partial loss is subluxation.

questions.q: Increased pressure inside the eye with sudden painful red eye, halos around lights and vomiting suggests:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. An emergency.

questions.q: The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme covers all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. TB has its own National TB Elimination Programme.

questions.q: The safe disposal of human excreta in rural areas is promoted under:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Toilets and an end to open defecation.

questions.q: The characteristic smell of bitter almonds at autopsy suggests poisoning by:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Not everyone can detect it.
